title: ephemeral-oncall-workflow-bridge-and-telemetry-sampler
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: on-call workflows today are tightly coupled to long-lived runbook attachments and heavy telemetry dumps; responders often need a lightweight, ephemeral context that follows an incident lifecycle without creating long-lived artifacts. This PR introduces two cooperating pieces: (1) an Ephemeral Oncall Workflow Bridge that attaches a short-lived 'workflow context' to incidents and automatically expires after a TTL, and (2) a Telemetry Sampler CLI + server-side sampler that captures compact diagnostic envelopes (trace spans, sampled logs, key metrics) at controlled sample rates for fast triage.

What changed: added a small bridge microservice that can be triggered by the incident-bot or SLO alert pipelines to create/update a workflow context object (metadata + ephemeral note stream + short-lived temporary links). The bridge exposes a REST endpoint and a lightweight proto for clients. The telemetry sampler implements rate-limited sampling, field redaction hooks, and an opt-out header to ensure we never capture PII or sensitive headers. A new command-line tool (slo-sampler) allows on-call to request an immediate sample from a target service/trace id and attach the compact envelope to the workflow context.

Design notes: workflow contexts are stored in Redis with signed tokens for short-lived access; full historical artifacts remain in the long-term diagnostics bucket only if explicitly promoted by an engineer. Sampler uses deterministic hashing on trace id + incident id to allow reproducible sampling policies. Default sample rate is conservative (0.02) and can be overridden by policy. The bridge is intentionally minimal: no external UI changes were made in this PR; integration points are via incident-bot annotations and a small webhook that the Console can consume later.

Security & privacy: added KMS-backed signing for ephemeral tokens; sampling has a strict redaction pipeline configurable in environment variables. Default redaction removes headers matching Authorization/Cookie and scrubs email-like tokens. A short security review checklist is included in tests.

Tests & rollout: unit tests for sampler logic and bridge handlers included, e2e smoke harness that runs against a local dockerized Redis and sample backend. Rollout plan is staged: enable bridge in dev, opt-in beta in staging via feature flag, then roll to production with gradually increasing sample rates. Rollback is a feature-flag disable.

Why it matters: responders get fast, contextual diagnostic snapshots without creating large long-lived dumps; platform teams can tune costs via sample rate and promote only important captures to longer retention.

Notes: this description is intentionally compact; see changed_files for code pointers and the commits list for granular changes.
